svg.text: Everything here works on each rank's own A and B tiles (panel 2 of the tiling scheme). Stage 1 picks a power-of-two shift per row of A and per column of B, so the scaled,
truncated integers are small enough for the CRT with num_moduli moduli; it needs the row and column communicators and one small int8 GEMM. Stage 2 turns the scaled tiles into
one int8 residue plane per modulus, with no communication. par and par::async run the same code for both stages.
A row-wise and B column-wise, in the order the kernels run (src/par/par_scaling.cu). Circled numbers match the notes below.
① ② A tile holds only part of each row of A (and a B tile part of each column of B), so the local amax is max-reduced across the ranks holding the rest (panel 2). shift = max_ufp − ilogb(amax).

③ extract_bound writes an int8 upper bound of |A|·2^shift into l_A_lo (and of B into l_B_lo), k-major with k padded to a multiple of 256. It occupies plane 0 until stage 2 overwrites it with residues.
④ The bound GEMM estimates how large each entry of the scaled product can get. It is the only step in stages 1–2 that needs another rank's data (panel 3). C_hi is zeroed first.
⑤ ⑥ Row maxima of C_hi refine shiftA and column maxima refine shiftB, again reduced over the row / column communicator, so every entry of the product fits the CRT range of num_moduli moduli.
⑦ trunc_core applies the final shifts and truncates: A_core / B_core hold the integer-valued scaled tiles, k-major, leading dimension padding(l_kA) / padding(l_kB).
2 · Why the reductions use the row and column communicators
A row of A (and of C_hi) is split across the two ranks in its grid row; a column of B (and of C_hi) across the two ranks in its grid column. The shaded band is one such row or column.
row of A → ranks 0, 2: row comm
column of B → ranks 0, 1: col comm
rows: row comm · columns: col comm
Each reduction is an in-place NCCL max over a vector of per-row (l_m) or per-column (l_n) maxima on a 2-rank communicator: rows need no column communication and vice versa.
After ② and ⑥ both ranks in a grid row hold identical shiftA for their rows, and both ranks in a grid column identical shiftB, so the tiles they later exchange are scaled consistently.
3 · The bound GEMM ④: two K-strips with peer exchanges
matmult::two_round_peer_gemm_i8 (include/par/par_matmult.hpp). Rank (prow, pcol) computes its C_hi tile as the sum of two K-strips: C_hi = A(prow, 0)·B(0, pcol) + A(prow, 1)·B(1, pcol). It
holds one operand of each strip; the other comes from a peer.
Exchange (one NCCL sendrecv each, overlapped on their own streams): A_bound tile ↔ row peer (rank ^ 2) into packA_recv; B_bound tile ↔ col peer (rank ^ 1) into packB_recv.

The k-strips line up because A's k split (by pcol) and B's k split (by prow) use the same rule: strip 0 is the first k block (which takes the remainder) in both, so the two operands of each strip have the
Diagonal ranks 0 and 3 start one strip from purely local data while the exchanges are in flight; the edge ranks 1 and 2 need one peer tile for each strip, so they wait before both.
The GEMM is on the int8 bounds, not on residues: it runs once, at tile size (l_m × l_n × l_k), whatever num_moduli is.
ozaki::moduli_expand, called by moduli_expand_local (src/par/par_moduli.cu). Each element of A_core becomes num_moduli int8 residues, one per modulus p_i, written to plane i of l_A_lo. Same for
16 int8 planes, each padding(l_kA) × l_m, stride l_A_plane_elems; colour = rank that owns modulus i

Every rank expands its own tile for all num_moduli moduli, though it keeps only its own share: stage 3 then sends plane range [q_begin, q_begin + q_count) of the tile to rank q (panel 3 of the tiling scheme),
so the colours here are the owners from dist::moduli_range.
No communication in stage 2. The planes keep A_core's k-major layout and padding, which is why stage 3's unpack drops the k-padding when it places a tile into the full A_lo[j] plane.
l_A_lo is also where ③ put the int8 bound tile; stage 2 overwrites it. B is identical with l_B_lo, padding(l_kB) × l_n planes (written four int8 at a time as char4).
